title: What Is Native Advertising? Benefits, Types, and Tips

facts.fact: The page cites a third-party source (ReadPeak) stating that the average click-through rate for banner ads has fallen to approximately 0.35%.
The page states that over 80% of users either completely ignore banner ads or use ad-blocking tools to avoid them, based on unnamed studies it says 'indicate' this.
facts.quote: with over 80% of users just completely ignoring them or use ad-blocking tools to avoid them altogether

facts.fact: The page states that studies have shown native ads generate up to 8.8 times more click-throughs than traditional banner ads, without naming the studies.
facts.unit: times more click-throughs than banner ads (up to)
facts.quote: Studies have shown that native ads generate up to 8.8 times more click-throughs than traditional banner ads.

facts.fact: The page defines native advertising as paid content that matches the look, feel, and function of the media in which it appears, and says this is the definition NAI follows.
facts.quote: Native Advertising is paid content that matches the look, feel, and function of the media in which it appears.

facts.fact: The page states that the concept of native advertising can trace its roots back to the 1940s, when print ads were designed to blend into newspaper and magazine editorial content.
facts.quote: It can trace its roots back to the 1940s,

facts.fact: The page is dated August 27, 2026 and is labeled as a 2026 updated guide.
